$comment: Reason ids the library can report, strongest first: a verdict lists its reasons in this order. Ids are a public contract: added, never renamed within a major version. half: where the evidence is read. names: whether the reason can name an agent (signer, token, page-declaration, a product name) or never does (null).

reasons.summary: A Web Bot Auth signature on the request verified against a key bundled with this release.
The hosting platform verified the request as a known bot (Cloudflare's verified-bot category).
The request carries a Web Bot Auth signature that did not verify here: an unknown or expired key, a signature outside its window, or a check that failed.
The user agent contains a token that declares software: an agent, fetcher, crawler, link previewer or HTTP client.
The page's own navigator declares a hosted browser engine.
navigator.webdriver is true: the browser declares that automation controls it.
The user agent declares headless Chrome.
The credential methods are replaced by the accessor family Muse's cloud browser installs.
The credential methods are wrapped the way Instinct's cloud desktop wraps them; counts only together with the GeeTest pair.
The GeeTest initialisers are the accessor pair Instinct installs; counts only together with the credential wrappers.
window.prompt has the Codex in-app browser's shape; counts only with a second Codex shell signal.
The keyboard layout map is empty, as in the Codex in-app browser; counts only with a second Codex shell signal.
The Codex in-app browser's overlay is attached to the document; counts only with a second Codex shell signal.
ChatGPT for Chrome's activity badge was drawn on the page while its agent acted.
Claude for Chrome's activity marker was drawn on the page while its agent acted.
Trusted input arrived while the document was hidden yet reported focus, which needs focus emulation.
A trusted pointerdown arrived while the document was hidden, which no person can produce.
